findings.title: unsubscribe action crashes for users without a TopicUser record
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by may return nil when the user has never interacted with the topic (e.g., an email link clicked by a user who was notified but has no row). `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a graceful response.

findings.title: unsubscribe is a state-changing GET reachable without login and without CSRF protection
findings.body: The unsubscribe route is a GET that mutates notification_level, and ensure_logged_in is applied, but current_user is nil for anonymous requests, so current_user.id raises. More importantly, state-changing GET requests are triggered by link prefetchers/mail scanners and are CSRF-able; the action also toggles between muted and regular rather than being idempotent, so repeated prefetch flips the setting back and forth.

findings.title: TopicView.new called without guardian scope; access check missing for private topics
findings.body: TopicView is built with current_user but the subsequent update applies to any topic_id the user can construct; if TopicView raises NotFound/InvalidAccess the rescue in show is not present here, so errors leak as unhandled exceptions. Also no check that the topic is visible to the user before mutating its TopicUser.

findings.title: Toggle logic inverts intent and can unmute/stop incorrectly
findings.body: If notification_level is above regular (e.g., watching/tracking) it is lowered to regular, otherwise it is set to muted. Clicking the link for a regular user mutes the topic, but for a muted user it stays muted with no way to re-enable via this link; behaviour is unclear and not idempotent for the unsubscribe semantics described in the UI text.

findings.title: Placeholders are no longer wrapped in HTML elements consistently; %{unsubscribe_link} line depends on a template variable never supplied to the ERB
findings.body: The template contains %{respond_instructions} and %{unsubscribe_link} placeholders, which are only substituted in MessageBuilder#html_part when add_unsubscribe_link is set. Any caller rendering this template without that option (or the substitution order) leaves raw %{...} text in the email.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now always includes the per-topic link, but the plain-text body text is built from the same key
findings.body: The unsubscribe_link string now requires %{unsubscribe_url}. Callers that invoke I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) without unsubscribe_url (e.g., digest emails or other add_unsubscribe_link paths) will get an interpolation error or a literal '%{unsubscribe_url}' in the outgoing text.

findings.title: unsubscribe_url uses post.topic.unsubscribe_url which points at the non-slug-less route with an extra segment
findings.body: Topic#unsubscribe_url returns "#{url}/unsubscribe" where url includes the post number only when >1; for post_number>1 this yields /t/slug/id/5/unsubscribe, which matches no route (the unsubscribe routes are /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe), so the link 404s.

findings.title: Misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: The property is spelled 'stopNotificiationsText' here and in the template; while consistent, the typo propagates into the public API of the controller and is easy to break when someone fixes one occurrence only.

findings.title: Strings used in the unsubscribe page are inserted with triple-stash HTML from a translation
findings.body: stop_notifications contains <strong> and the template renders it with {{{...}}} with the topic fancyTitle interpolated unescaped into the I18n string, allowing HTML injection from topic titles into the page.

findings.title: unsubscribe_url may be built from a stale or unslugged url
findings.body: unsubscribe_url interpolates url which includes slug; for topics where slug is recomputed lazily this can differ from the route that the controller redirects to, causing redirect loops with the slug mismatch check.

findings.title: No tests for the new per-topic unsubscribe behaviour in the controller or mailer
findings.body: The only change is to pass unsubscribe_url into a builder spec that never asserts on it. The new TopicsController#unsubscribe action, the redirect logic, the toggle semantics and the new unsubscribe_link text have no specs.
